editorial:
You find yourself walking through a never-ending subway tunnel with no way out. Exit 8 puts you right in the shoes of a regular guy who gets stuck in a strange, repeating hallway. The rules are simple but terrifying: spot anything weird and turn back, or keep moving if everything looks normal. One mistake sends him right back to the start. The movie does a great job making you feel trapped right alongside him, with clean white walls and flickering lights that make every step feel heavy. You never know what strange thing might pop up next, and that constant guessing keeps you on edge the whole time.

The acting carries the whole film, especially since it's mostly one person alone in a hallway. The pacing is tight and never drags, with each loop feeling different enough to stay interesting. On the downside, some viewers might find the repetitive structure tiring after a while, and the ending may leave you with more questions than answers. Still, if you love puzzle-style thrillers that mess with your head, this is right up your alley. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the man finally notices a subtle anomaly he missed before, a small detail that changes everything. He turns back one last time and the hallway finally shifts. Instead of looping, the path opens up to a real exit. He steps through and finds himself back in the normal world, but the twist reveals that the subway station was never real. It was a test, and passing it means he was chosen for something bigger. The screen cuts to black as he walks into the sunlight, leaving you wondering what comes next.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves mind-bending puzzle thrillers and single-location horror stories.
